proposals.relationship: Shapin identifies Kuhn’s Structure of Scientific Revolutions as a major formative reading that presented science-making as a human endeavor.
proposals.evidence_note: Own2024recollection,published2025,4–5 explicitly distinguishes encountering books from knowing their authors. Koestler and C.P.Snow retain credit as other important undergraduate readings; Kuhn is not a sole influence or an inferred supervisor. The original Structure edition remains unread by this dossier.

proposals.relationship: Questions the internalist/externalist division associated with Kuhn’s1968 history-of-science essay, treating the boundary itself as a historical problem.
proposals.evidence_note: Own2024reply,published2025,7 contrasts the inherited framing with the joint Air-Pump project’s approach; Schaffer retains credit. Shapin also calls Kuhn’s account of Polanyi insufficiently appreciative on10. These particular reservations coexist with explicit formative debt; no blanket rejection or claim of reading the complete1968essay,1992paper or2011introduction.

proposals.relationship: Credits Goffman’s frontstage/backstage sensibilities with accompanying much of his work on how scientific performances are made.
proposals.evidence_note: Own2024recollection,published2025,10 names The Presentation of Self in Everyday Life and explains the relevance to recovering practices hidden by polished accounts. A specified intellectual debt, not personal contact or a claim that science is merely theatrical deception. Cited original book unread.

proposals.relationship: Uses Douglas’s account of shared thought to explain why social relations are constitutive of knowledge rather than an external influence.
proposals.evidence_note: Own2024reply,published2025,11 interprets a remark from Implicit Meanings,1975,xx, while also crediting conversations with Barnes and Bloor. A particular conceptual resource, not wholesale adoption of Douglas or denial of scientific knowledge. Original book unread.

proposals.relationship: Daston uses Shapin’s interpretation of Merton and his work on experimental witnessing and trust while developing her account of scientific moral economies (1995).
proposals.evidence_note: Own Daston5/n8 and14–15/nn34–37. Merton’s social-standing problem is distinguished from the content of knowledge; gentlemanly trust helps explain collaborative empiricism. The joint Shapin/Schaffer Air-Pump study and Hannaway’s separate work retain credit. This is Daston’s specified use, not sole authorship of her program; complete cited originals unread.
